headline: Who will take Misti’s seat in Parliament? BNP veterans and grassroots leaders vie for vacant seat

members.title: Election schedule announced for by-election to reserved seat vacated by Ferdousi Ahmed
members.lead: The Election Commission (EC) has announced the schedule for the by-election to the reserved women’s seat in the 13th National Parliament, which fell vacant following the resignation of Ferdousi Ahmed Mishti. A notification to this effect was issued on Monday, signed by EC Secretary Akhtar Ahmed. According to the announced schedule, nomination papers must be submitted to the returning officer at the Nirbachan Bhaban (Election Commission building) by 26 October. The nomination papers will be scrutinised on 27 October, and the last date for withdrawal of candidacies is 1 November. Voting will take place on 12 November. . Ferdousi Ahmed was a Member of Parliament elected to a reserved women’s seat nominated by the BNP. Under the law, only the BNP can nominate a candidate for the vacant seat. If there is more than one candidate, only MPs from the BNP alliance will be eligible to vote. However, reserved women’s seats are generally contested by a single candidate, making a vote unnecessary. Ferdousi Ahmed Mishti was accused of being involved in an attack, looting and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Dhaka’s Mirpur. On 1 October, she resigned as a Member of Parliament on the instructions of party chief and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

members.title: Who will take Misti’s seat in Parliament? BNP veterans and grassroots leaders vie for vacant seat
members.lead: Following Ferdousi Ahmed Misti’s resignation, speculation has begun among the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leaders, activists and supporters over who will fill the vacant reserved seat for women in Parliament. Former members of parliament (MPs) and senior central leaders are already lobbying for the nomination, while district-level organisers are also making efforts to secure the party’s backing. Many of those seeking the nomination had failed to secure a reserved seat this time. Some had also competed for the party’s nomination in the directly contested parliamentary election. They believe Misti’s resignation has opened up a new opportunity for them. Senior BNP leaders say the party is now in power, making a seat in Parliament under the ruling party’s banner particularly attractive. Beyond the familiar faces among its women leaders, many others are also seeking the nomination, approaching senior central leaders at their offices and homes. The party, however, has yet to decide whom it will select, but the vacancy has generated considerable interest among leaders at various levels, including the Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal, the BNP’s women’s wing. . Misti came under scrutiny over political accountability after people close to her were linked to an attack, looting and the demolition of a building at the Radda Health Centre in Mirpur, Dhaka. Following instructions from Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman, she submitted her resignation to Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad on 1 October. Misti, however, has denied allegations of involvement in the attack and vandalism. This resignation of Ferdousi Ahmed Misti has left one reserved seat for women vacant. Under the existing system, parties are allocated reserved seats for women in proportion to the number of directly elected MPs they have in Parliament.
